overview: NextEra Energy is one of the largest electric power and energy infrastructure companies in North America, operating through two principal businesses: Florida Power & Light (FPL), the largest rate-regulated electric utility in Florida and the U.S. by retail MWh sales, serving over 6 million customer accounts; and NextEra Energy Resources (NEER), one of the largest generators of renewable (wind and solar) energy and battery storage in the world, which develops, builds and operates long-term contracted generation, storage, and transmission assets across the U.S. and Canada. The company had approximately 80 GW of net generation and storage capacity as of year-end 2025, and in May 2026 agreed to acquire Dominion Energy in an all-stock, roughly $67 billion merger that would create the largest U.S. regulated utility by rate base.

business_model.summary: A dual-engine model combining a cost-of-service regulated utility (FPL) that earns a government-authorized return on a growing rate base, with a competitive/contracted infrastructure developer (NEER) that earns long-term contracted cash flows from renewables, storage, nuclear and gas assets sold under ~14-year average power purchase agreements (PPAs). FPL revenue is largely a pass-through/cost-recovery model (fuel clauses, storm clauses) plus a regulated base-rate return (authorized ROE of 10.95%, range 9.95%-11.95%, under the 2025 rate agreement effective January 2026-December 2029); NEER revenue is substantially contracted (~95% of net generating capacity under long-term contracts) with a smaller merchant/trading component (customer supply, gas and power marketing).

revenue_streams.name: FPL (regulated utility - base rates, cost-recovery clauses, retail/wholesale electric sales)
NEER (contracted renewables, storage, nuclear, gas generation and transmission)
Customer supply / marketing, trading and gas & oil production

business_model.customer_type: Mixed: FPL is B2C/B2B retail and wholesale electricity (12 million people, 6M+ customer accounts, >30 franchise agreements); NEER is B2B - utilities, retail electricity providers, power cooperatives, municipal electric providers, and increasingly large-load industrial/data-center customers under long-term PPAs and emerging large-load tariffs
business_model.geographic_mix: FPL: Florida only (east/lower west coasts and 10 northwest Florida counties). NEER: 44 U.S. states and 4 Canadian provinces, with generation concentrated in Texas, the West and Midwest (wind) and West/South regions (solar); regulated gas pipelines in the Southeast/Appalachia; regulated electric transmission in SPP, ERCOT, CAISO, NYISO, MISO and PJM footprints

competitive_position.market_position: Largest U.S. electric utility by market capitalization (~$180-200B) and one of the largest renewable energy generators/developers globally; FPL is the largest electric utility in Florida and the U.S. by customer count; NEER is the largest wholesale generator of wind and battery storage capacity in the U.S.

moat_factors.description: 226 franchise agreements (typically 30-year terms) and FPSC-regulated territorial monopoly give FPL a durable, low-risk earnings base with an authorized ROE and multi-year rate certainty through 2029
FPL's low-cost position (natural gas, solar, nuclear mix) keeps customer bills below the cost of self-generation for most customers, reducing competitive/self-generation threats

moat_factors.factor: Development and execution track record / supply chain scale
moat_factors.description: NEER's scale, creditworthiness, operating history and project-execution reputation are cited by the company itself as key competitive advantages in winning PPAs against smaller developers
~95% of NEER capacity under long-term contracts (avg. ~14 years remaining) and a ~36.7 GW development backlog (as of Q3 2026) provide revenue visibility years in advance

Investment-grade credit ratings and scale give NEE/FPL/NEECH favorable capital market access versus smaller renewable developers, though this is eroding somewhat as leverage rises with the capex buildout

moat_factors.factor: Capital recycling vehicle (XPLR Infrastructure, formerly NextEra Energy Partners)
moat_factors.description: Affiliated yieldco-style vehicle provides a channel to monetize operating assets and recycle capital into new development, though XPLR's own cost of capital has risen materially

weaknesses: Geographic concentration of FPL in a single, hurricane-prone state exposes a majority of regulated earnings to Florida-specific regulatory, political and weather risk
Heavy reliance on renewable tax credits (PTC/ITC) that are being phased out/restricted under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), with no credits for wind/solar placed in service after 2030
NEER's merchant and trading exposure (limited but present) introduces commodity price and counterparty risk not present in a pure regulated utility
Interest expense has risen sharply (NEE consolidated interest expense roughly doubled from 2024 to 2025) as the company funds an enormous growth capex program, pressuring GAAP earnings

Pending ~$67B Dominion Energy acquisition introduces integration, multi-state regulatory approval (Virginia, North and South Carolina, FERC, NRC) and execution risk, and the market's initial negative share-price reaction signals skepticism about near-term dilution

growth_drivers: Explosive data center and AI-driven electricity demand: NEE is in active discussions on 30 large-load energy supply hubs (expected to grow to ~40 by year-end 2026) and has signed federal data-center hub agreements covering up to ~16.5 GW

FPL rate base growth under the 2025 rate agreement (2026-2029), including new base rate increases of $945M (2026) and $705M (2027), plus a Solar and Battery Base Rate Adjustment (SoBRA) mechanism for projects entering service 2027-2029, and large-load tariffs for new customers ≥50 MW with ≥85% load factor
NEER's renewables/storage development backlog of ~36.7 GW (as of Q3 2026, including ~2.4 GW of battery storage added in the quarter alone) supporting long-term contracted earnings growth
Battery storage buildout - NEER is a world leader in battery storage capacity and continues to add GW-scale storage both standalone and co-located with solar/wind to firm intermittent generation

Pending acquisition of Dominion Energy (~$67B all-stock deal announced May 2026) would create the largest U.S. regulated utility by rate base (~$138B combined), adding Virginia/Carolinas data-center-rich service territory and additional transmission investment opportunity
Nuclear fleet optionality - restart of the Duane Arnold nuclear plant (targeted ~2029 commercial operation) backed by a 25-year PPA, capturing demand for firm, carbon-free baseload power
FPL capital expenditure program of roughly $90-100 billion through 2032 across generation, storage, transmission and distribution
Use of AI and proprietary technology tools across FPL and NEER operations to lower costs and improve grid/field efficiency, supporting both margin and reliability improvements
Acquisition of Symmetry Energy Solutions (January 2026) expanding NEER's commercial and industrial natural gas marketing business
Long-term management target of 8%+ adjusted EPS CAGR off the 2025 base (~$3.71) through the early-2030s, alongside ~10% dividend growth guided for 2026 and ~6%/year dividend growth from 2026-2028

business.description: FPL's service territory covers the hurricane-prone Florida coasts; 2026 saw Hurricane Isaias knock out power to ~435,000 FPL customers, requiring a ~17,000-person restoration workforce; storm costs are recoverable only via interim surcharges capped (currently at $5 per 1,000 kWh in the first 12 months) and subject to FPSC prudence review, creating timing/recovery risk

FPL and NEER results depend on continued growth in customer accounts and usage (including from data centers); a slowdown in economic activity, population growth or large-load commitments not materializing (FPL currently has no signed large-load/data-center customer under its new tariff per some analyst commentary) could leave planned capex under-utilized

Four FPL and three NEER nuclear units (plus the Duane Arnold restart) carry outage, decommissioning-funding, and regulatory (NRC) risk; unplanned outages or failure to secure license renewals could be materially adverse

Large renewables/storage/transmission backlog (~36.7 GW) and the Duane Arnold restart depend on timely permitting, supply chain availability (batteries, turbines, transformers) and labor; delays or cost overruns can reduce or eliminate expected returns and tax credit eligibility

The pending ~$67B all-stock acquisition requires FERC, NRC, Virginia SCC, North Carolina and South Carolina regulatory approvals over an expected 12-18 month timeline; deal could be modified, delayed, or burdened with customer-concession conditions, and carries integration/execution risk and reciprocal termination fees up to $6.52B

financial.description: Consolidated interest expense roughly doubled from $2,235M (2024) to $4,572M (2025) as NEE funds its capex program with debt; GAAP net income attributable to NEE fell from $6,946M (2024) to $6,835M (2025) and diluted EPS fell from $3.37 to $3.30 even as adjusted/operating metrics grew

NEE, NEECH and FPL rely on regular access to debt and equity markets to fund ~$90-100B of FPL capex through 2032 plus NEER's development backlog; disruption, higher-for-longer rates, or credit rating pressure would raise financing costs or force delayed/reduced investment

NEE is a holding company dependent on subsidiary dividends/distributions; project-specific non-recourse financing defaults, joint-venture partner issues, or ratings downgrades (which can trigger collateral posting) could pressure liquidity

financial.risk: XPLR Infrastructure (affiliated yieldco) cost of capital
financial.description: XPLR (formerly NEP) has had to raise capital at high cost (~7.75% reported), which can limit its usefulness as a capital-recycling outlet for NEER assets

regulatory.description: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act and related IRS guidance (August 2025) tightened the 'begin construction' test and set a hard cutoff: no PTC/ITC for wind or solar facilities placed in service after 2030, raising costs and risk for NEER's development pipeline

regulatory.risk: FPL rate case / regulatory lag risk
regulatory.description: FPL's earnings depend on FPSC approval of base rates and cost recovery; the FPSC can disallow costs it deems imprudent, and the January 2026 final order approving the 2025 rate agreement is already being challenged by intervenors (Office of Public Counsel and others) via a motion for reconsideration

The Dominion acquisition requires multi-jurisdictional approval (FERC Section 203, NRC, HSR antitrust review, Virginia SCC, North and South Carolina commissions); any of these bodies could reject, delay, or impose costly conditions (e.g., incremental customer bill credits beyond the $2.25B already offered)

regulatory.risk: Federal/state policy shifts on wind/solar permitting
regulatory.description: A 2025 federal executive order paused federal land leasing/permitting for wind development pending review; similar actions could delay or block NEER projects
ESA/BGEPA compliance (e.g., a NEER subsidiary on probation for eagle collisions at wind facilities) and evolving greenhouse gas rules could raise costs or restrict operations

macro.description: As one of the most capital-intensive companies in the S&P 500 funding a multi-decade capex supercycle, NEE's cost of capital, equity issuance needs and valuation multiple are highly sensitive to the level and trajectory of long-term interest rates; several sell-side price target cuts in 2026 cited higher rates as a valuation headwind

Natural gas, oil and energy commodity prices affect FPL fuel costs (largely pass-through) and NEER's natural gas/oil production, customer supply and trading businesses; prolonged low gas/oil prices could impair E&P investments, while spikes raise working-capital/collateral needs
Utility demand is relatively defensive, but industrial/data-center load growth assumptions embedded in the backlog and large-load tariffs could soften in a broader economic slowdown

A meaningful share of the forward growth narrative (data-center hubs, large-load tariffs) depends on continued hyperscaler/AI infrastructure investment; any slowdown in AI-related data center buildout would reduce incremental demand NEE is counting on

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. electricity demand is inflecting upward after roughly two decades of flat demand, driven by data centers/AI, electrification (EVs, heat pumps) and reshoring of manufacturing; regulated utilities and renewable developers with scale, balance-sheet strength and permitted land/interconnection positions are best positioned to capture this demand, while tax-credit policy (OBBBA phase-outs) and interest rates are the dominant swing factors for renewables economics
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate. FPL's regulated earnings are largely non-cyclical (essential service, cost-of-service recovery); NEER's earnings are more cyclical/variable due to weather-driven wind/solar output variability and some commodity/merchant exposure, but are cushioned by long-term contracts
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - NEE is one of the most capital-intensive, debt-funded growth stories among large-cap utilities; equity/debt cost of capital directly affects project returns, EPS accretion math on the Dominion deal, and the stock's relative valuation versus bonds
key_input_costs: Steel, copper and other construction materials

recent_developments.event: Adjusted EPS of $1.24 beat estimates (~$1.18 expected); management reaffirmed full-year FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.92-$4.02 and said it is targeting the high end despite an expected weaker Q4 wind resource (90-95% of long-term average)

NEER added ~3.7 GW of new renewables/storage to its development backlog (2.4 GW of which was battery storage), bringing the total backlog to ~36.7 GW; active large-load/data-center hub discussions expected to grow from 30 to 40 by year-end 2026
FPL restored power to substantially all ~435,000 customers affected by Hurricane Isaias, mobilizing a workforce of roughly 17,000 for restoration

NextEra Energy announced an agreement to acquire Dominion Energy in an all-stock transaction valued at roughly $66.8-67.4 billion (0.8138 NextEra shares per Dominion share plus a $360 million one-time cash payment to Dominion holders at close), creating the largest U.S. regulated utility by combined rate base (~$138B); deal expected to close in 12-18 months pending FERC, NRC and Virginia/Carolinas regulatory approval; NEE shares fell roughly 4-6% on the announcement amid integration and dilution concerns

FPSC issued a final order approving the 2025 base rate agreement, effective January 2026 through December 2029, raising annualized base revenues by $945 million in 2026 and $705 million in 2027, with an authorized regulatory ROE of 10.95% (range 9.95%-11.95%); the order is being challenged by intervenors via a motion for reconsideration filed in February 2026
NEER (through NextEra Energy Resources) acquired Symmetry Energy Solutions, a commercial and industrial natural gas marketing business

IRS issued new 'begin construction' guidance under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act tightening eligibility for wind/solar PTC/ITC tax credits, eliminating the 5% safe harbor for projects beginning construction on or after September 2, 2025, and confirming no credits for projects placed in service after 2030
NEER submitted an NRC application to reinstate the operating license for the Duane Arnold nuclear plant, targeting a 2029 commercial operation date, backed by a 25-year PPA for its full output

items.notes: Management is targeting the high end of the range despite an expected below-average Q4 wind resource (90-95% of long-term average)

items.target: 8%+ CAGR off a 2025 adjusted EPS base (~$3.71)
items.period: through the early 2030s (through 2032/2035 per varying investor decks)
items.notes: Framing has broadened from an earlier 6-8% through-2027 target to 8%+ through a longer horizon as data-center demand visibility has improved

items.target: ~10% in 2026 (off a 2024 base), then ~6%/year from year-end 2026 through 2028
items.notes: Dividend growth is expected to step down from ~10% to ~6% annually after 2026
Supports FPL regulatory capital employed growth of roughly 8%/year; some reports suggest 2026 capex is tracking toward the low end (~$12B) of its range
Up from prior quarter after adding ~3.7 GW in Q3 2026 (2.4 GW of which was battery storage)

items.target: expected to grow from 30 to 40 active hubs
items.notes: Federal data-center hub agreements signed covering up to ~16.5 GW, up from 9.5 GW announced in April 2026

guidance.management_commentary: CEO John Ketchum emphasized the acceleration of data-center/AI-driven large-load demand as the central growth driver, framing the backlog growth and hub discussions as evidence of durable, multi-year visibility. Management continues to target the high end of FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance despite acknowledging a weaker-than-average Q4 wind resource. On the Dominion transaction, management has characterized the deal as immediately accretive and consistent with the long-term 8%+ EPS growth framework, while acknowledging the 12-18 month regulatory approval timeline across FERC, the NRC and Virginia/Carolinas state commissions.

bull_case: Best-positioned large-cap utility to capture the AI/data-center electricity demand supercycle, with ~36.7 GW of contracted development backlog and up to 40 large-load hubs in active discussion by year-end 2026

FPL's newly approved 2025 rate agreement (through 2029) provides multi-year earnings visibility with an attractive authorized ROE (10.95%) and built-in mechanisms (SoBRA, large-load tariffs) to capture incremental growth

Pending Dominion Energy acquisition would create the largest U.S. regulated utility by rate base, adding scale, Virginia data-center-corridor exposure, and additional transmission investment opportunity, management says accretive to EPS

Long-standing track record of 8%+ targeted adjusted EPS growth and historically consistent dividend growth, combined with the largest renewables/storage platform in the industry and continued battery storage leadership
Diversification between a low-risk regulated utility (FPL) and a higher-growth contracted/competitive developer (NEER) provides balance between earnings stability and growth optionality
bear_case: Heavy, rising reliance on debt to fund a ~$90-100B+ capex program has driven consolidated interest expense to roughly double year-over-year, pressuring GAAP earnings and making the stock acutely sensitive to higher-for-longer interest rates

The ~$67B Dominion Energy acquisition introduces significant integration, multi-state/multi-agency regulatory approval, and dilution risk over a 12-18 month timeline; the market's initial negative share-price reaction signals skepticism about near-term EPS optics and deal execution
OBBBA-driven phase-out of wind/solar tax credits (no credits for projects placed in service after 2030) raises costs and risk for a large share of NEER's development pipeline, a core growth driver

Concentrated exposure to Florida hurricane risk at FPL, with recovery of storm costs subject to regulatory caps, prudence review and potential disallowance, creating episodic earnings and cash-flow volatility

Data-center/large-load demand, the central bullish narrative, remains partly speculative - some reporting suggests FPL has yet to sign an actual data-center customer under its new large-load tariff, raising the risk that near-term growth expectations outrun contracted reality
